claim_text: The analysis assumes support on a union of M low-dimensional linear subspaces, zero mass on their pairwise intersections, non-trivial component mass, and only subgaussian tails within each subspace.
paper_dependency_under_test: Appendix B.1 Lemma 3 asserts that Assumption 1 alone permits exact recovery of every declared subspace with failure probability O(M n^-10) from O(c_p^2 M^2 (k+1) log n) samples.
domain: All target distributions satisfying Assumption 1; Assumption 2 is also checked to keep the witness inside the theorem domain.
quantifiers: For every such target and sufficiently large n, one data-only algorithm using upper bounds on M and k succeeds with the stated probability.
falsification_criterion: Exhibit two distinct valid parameterizations with identical sample laws and disjoint exact-recovery targets, so at least one has success probability at most 1/2 for every n, contradicting a universal O(n^-10) failure bound for sufficiently large n.
non_circularity: No sample size, tolerance, or budget is selected from the theorem rate; the contradiction holds for every sample size.
